description: Two objects called the neutron-minus-proton element of H_3(q) agree classically but differ 39% at the substrate, with no disambiguation row in the corpus.
verdict: FLAG, not a verdict. chi_(3)(Delta_T_beta)/eps(Delta) -> 1 as q -> 1 but is 1.3909 at the substrate. Since the counit IS the lambda=(n) block, that ratio would be identically 1 for one and the same element, so the two objects the corpus calls the neutron-minus-proton element of H_3 are DIFFERENT -- agreeing classically, diverging 39% at q0, and both linear in hbar_q at leading order (which is why a leading-order check missed it). That is what two different q-deformations of one classical object look like, and is NOT automatically an error. What IS a defect is that no registry section-2 disambiguation row exists and nothing in the corpus states they differ, while Delta_tau_M and tr_M(Delta) feed different consumers. Settling it needs the two WORDS exhibited; not attempted here. Nothing wired.
